label: prose:intro-model-and-measurement
html:
Everything described so far is mathematics. The words electron, proton, mass and binding energy name constructions inside the model, and a statement about them is a statement about those constructions. The physical content of the paper is located in one place: where a quantity computed in the model is set beside a measured one — the CODATA fundamental constants, the Particle Data Group tables, the AME2020 atomic-mass evaluation. Those comparisons are the empirical claims, and the Physical Observations chapter collects them.

Three measured numbers are admitted, and only three. They are the calibration inputs, and they match one for one the three real degrees of freedom of the first cohomology of the genus-four state space (calibration–cohomology alignment; three calibration inputs):

  • the electron mass m_e fixes the unit of mass, the scale;
  • the neutron \beta-decay channel fixes the substrate parameter q_0, the modulus; because that modulus is overdetermined, its numerical value is read off the most precisely measured mass ratio available;
  • the pion channel fixes the one remaining orthogonal class, the meson scale.

Nothing else is fitted. In particular no object — a knot, a partition, a truncation order — is chosen because it reproduces a measured value; such a choice would be a fourth calibration in disguise (calibration discipline; epistemic status of the calibrations). Because m_e sets the unit by fiat, an absolute mass in MeV carries no information beyond the dimensionless ratio behind it, so the comparisons are made on ratios, binding energies, decay Q-values and mass splittings; the same boundary separates dimensionless \mathbb{Q}(q) clock grains and state-space moduli from empirical Compton and SI Planck length bridges (stratified spacetime, length, and distance scales).

The standard applied to each comparison is strict: a prediction is counted as meeting its target only when its residual is below one hundredth of the experimental uncertainty. The observations chapter reports every residual against that standard, including the misses, which at present are the majority. A derived quantity that misses is reported as a miss rather than tuned away, because only an untuned model can be corrected by what its errors teach.
